name: fs-scope-deny-mirror
body:
The acting agent's effective `edit`-action scope is the ordered combination of its opencode 2.x permission rules: the lower-priority configuration loads first, the global rules are appended next, and the agent's own rules are appended last, with the last matching rule winning — an allow rule grants the path and a deny rule revokes it. The fs tools' per-path scope (`apg_rm`/`apg_mv`/`apg_cp`) mirrors that ordered `edit` rule set because the tool asserts the `edit` action with the resolved path as the resource and opencode evaluates the whole rule set including `deny` entries, per `requirements.constraint.agent-fs-per-path-permission`; `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.fsScopeDecision` resolves the candidate's boundary frame. A code-writer path that resolves into the main checkout is refused independently, and `external_directory` governs an out-of-worktree path.

A deny rule that is the LAST matching rule refuses the operation exactly as `edit` does, so the template's sibling cross-denial (`deny a sibling's apg/.worktrees/*/src/golib/**`) is honoured by the fs tools. The unit/int tier pins the allow-success and deny-refusal cases against a faked V2 tool context; `opencode-suite/tools/apg_rm.ts`, `apg_mv.ts`, and `apg_cp.ts` consume the shared decision, and `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` describes the fs tools' scope as the effective allow-plus-deny scope with last match wins.
